Low milk supply happens when a mother doesn’t produce enough breast milk to meet her baby’s needs. Some signs are the baby not gaining enough weight, having fewer wet diapers, or being hungry after feeding. Many factors can affect milk supply, and it’s important to know the signs and ways to boost it, like utilizing a breast pump to increase milk supply . In this article, you will learn the best of the best pumps to increase your milk supply.
Low milk supply can happen for many reasons. It is often related to how breastfeeding starts and how it is managed. According to the UNICEF Organization , some reasons why you have a low milk supply are delays in breastfeeding, not enough skin-to-skin contact, or issues during delivery that can affect how quickly milk comes in.
Feeding issues, like poor latch, short feeds, or sticking to a strict schedule instead of feeding when the baby is hungry, can also reduce milk supply. Skipping night feeds and not feeding often enough are other common causes. Producing a low milk supply can also be caused by taking certain birth control pills or other medicines, drinking alcohol, smoking, or insufficient sleep.
Understanding this and taking action is the most appropriate thing to do. Pumping or expressing your milk frequently using the best breast pump for low supply between nursing sessions and consistently when you’re away from your baby can help build your milk supply.
The key to increasing milk supply is always emptying your breasts. It lets your body know that there is a demand, and thus, your body will produce more to meet that. The best way to do it is through breastfeeding, but that is not always an option. You may need to empty your breast while your baby is still full or asleep. This is where breast pumps come in. They allow you to express milk in these situations and store the supply for later use.
With that said, you should have a consistent pumping schedule. Ideally, you want to pump 8 - 12 times within 24 hours. This helps ensure that your breasts are never full and milk production does not stop.
The correct pump helps maximize milk expression by providing efficiency, customizable settings, and comfort. When selecting the best pump for a low milk supply, several critical factors must be considered, including function and fit.
High suction strength - The best pump for low milk supply should have a high suction strength for efficient milk expression. Higher suction strength helps to stimulate milk production and ensures that you can effectively empty your breasts, which can lead to increased milk supply over time. Look for the breast pump for low milk supply with adjustable suction levels to customize the intensity according to your comfort and needs.
Electric pumps - Electric pumps are often more effective than the best manual breast pump for low milk supply for frequent and consistent use. They offer steady and dependable suctions without the need for physical exertion. The best electric breast pump for low milk supply offers various settings to mimic a baby’s natural feeding pattern.
Double - The best pump to increase milk supply should have a double-pumping , enabling simultaneous milk expression on both breasts. Double pumping can also enhance let-down reflexes and improve milk flow.
Comfortable - A well-fitting flange is the best pump to in

crease milk supply. Flanges that are the correct size and shape for your breasts can prevent discomfort and ensure a proper seal, which helps to maximize milk flow. Since comfort is also key during the feedings that follow your pumping sessions, using a nursing pillow can provide the necessary ergonomic support to bottle-feed your baby without straining your arms or back.
Portable - Choose the best wearable breast pump for a low milk supply that is easy to carry and use wherever you go. To increase your milk supply, you must pump often; a compact and lightweight pump can simplify your daily routine.
Quiet - A breast pump for a low milk supply that runs quietly can help you feel more relaxed during pumping sessions. Less noise can make the experience more comfortable and help with low milk flow.
Easy to clean - Choose the best breast pump for increasing supply that is simple to take apart and clean. Easy-to-clean parts make it faster to keep everything hygienic and reduce time spent on maintenance.
Premium Feature (Warm-Massage Breast Pump) - If you have trouble with milk letdown or flowing slowly, look for special features. A warm-massage breast pump , like the Momcozy W1 , uses gentle warmth and rhythmic massage to relax you. This helps your body release the hormone (oxytocin) that makes milk come out. Using both together is great for getting the most milk and building up your supply, making it a top choice if you have low milk supply.

1. Should I keep pumping if no milk is coming out?
Yes, you should keep pumping even if no milk comes out first. Pumping regularly helps your body produce more milk. Make sure your chosen best pump to increase milk supply is working well, and if you’re still having trouble, ask a lactation consultant or doctor for help.
2. What breast pump is best for low milk supply?
The best breast pumps offer customizable settings, strong suction, and a comfortable fit can be particularly helpful for those dealing with low milk supply. One highly recommended pump and the best pump to increase milk supply is the Momcozy M9.
3. What is considered a low milk supply when pumping?
When pumping, the considered low milk supply is when you produce less than 3 to 4 ounces every 3 hours.
4. What does "hospital-grade" actually mean?
A hospital-grade pump , like the Momcozy V1 Pro, is designed with a very strong and durable motor. These pumps are made to be extra powerful and are often used to help moms build their milk supply quickly or to help those who need to pump many times a day.
5. Can I get hospital-grade power in a wearable pump?
Yes! Some advanced models, like the Momcozy V1 Pro Hospital-Grade Wearable Breast Pump , give you that extra strength without keeping you stuck in one spot. This means you can get a professional level of milk expression while still being able to move around your home.
6. Are hospital-grade pumps always the best for increasing milk supply?
Not

necessarily. While they have strong motors, "powerful" isn't the only way to increase supply. Some wearable pumps also offer hospital-grade suction power. Additionally, pumps like the Momcozy W1 use warmth and massage to relax the breast, which can trigger a faster let-down and help you collect more milk in a different, more comfortable way.
7. How do I know if my breast pump flange fits correctly?
A good flange fit means your nipple moves freely in the tunnel without rubbing against the sides. If you see redness, feel pain, or notice that your nipple is being pulled too far into the pump, you might need a different size. Using the right size helps you get more milk and keeps you comfortable.
8. Should pumping ever be painful?
Pumping should never hurt. If you feel pain, try lowering the suction level. More suction does not always mean more milk! You should also check your fit and try using warmth or massage—like the features found on the Momcozy W1—to make the session feel more natural.
9. How often should I replace my breast pump parts?
It is a good idea to check pump parts like the silicone valves and membranes every few weeks. If they look worn out, stretched, or torn, replace them with new ones. Fresh parts help the pump keep its strong suction so you can collect more milk.
10. How do I clean and maintain my breast pump?
Keeping your breast pump clean is very important for your health and your baby's safety. After every use, take apart all the pieces that touched your milk. Wash them well with warm, soapy water. Rinse them off and let them air dry completely before you put the pump back together. You can also wipe the main pump motor with a damp cloth to keep it clean. Taking good care of your pump helps it last longer and keeps germs away.
11. Can I move around while I pump?
Yes! Using a wearable pump like the Momcozy W1 or Air 1 allows you to stay active. Just make sure the pump is tucked securely in your bra so it doesn't shift, which ensures the fit stays correct and the suction remains steady while you move.
Overall, it is not your entire fault if you have a low milk supply, but it is your responsibility as a mother to give your baby the best possible nourishment and support.
